question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Nadine Morano (PPE) Subject:

In the wake of Azerbaijan’s military offensive in September 2023, which has led to the exodus of over 100 000 Nagorno‑Karabakh Armenians, a number of former political and military leaders in the region have been arrested and transferred to Baku. In January 2025, 15 former Artsakh leaders, among others, were tried before an Azerbaijani military tribunal, largely behind closed doors. A number of the defendants, including former president Arayik Harutyunyan, were sentenced to life imprisonment, while others received hefty prison sentences. These proceedings raise serious concerns about compliance with international standards, including as regards the fairness of the trial, access to defence and judicial transparency. In this context, the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy is asked to answer the following questions: 1.
What action does the Commission plan to take to ensure that the fundamental rights of these prisoners are respected?
Does it plan to ramp up its diplomatic efforts to secure their release or, at the very least, effective guarantees that their rights are respected?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.5.2026) The EU has closely followed the trials of Karabakh Armenians in Azerbaijan and has emphasised the importance of ensuring due process and the right to a fair trial, in line with international standards. The EU has also encouraged Azerbaijan and Armenia to address all outstanding humanitarian issues in the context of their bilateral normalisation process, including through confidence-building measures. Following the initialling of the bilateral peace treaty between Azerbaijan and Armenia on 8 August 2025, the parties have made important progress towards achieving lasting peace. This progress has already resulted in several tangible steps to the benefit of both counties, including the release of detainees and the lifting of trade and transit restrictions. The EU strongly supports this process and remains ready to continue to assist the parties in their efforts.
